["Ah, meu querido! Come here, come see what Avó has for us today. Look in the frigorífico! We have some lovely ovos, some bacalhau that's just waiting to be made delicious, and some good, honest batatas. And of course, a little cebola and some azeite.

Nossa Senhora!, this is going to be a simple, but ai que bom! recipe. We will make a beautiful **Bacalhau à Avó** – my way!

First, let's get our batatas ready. Wash them well, my darling, and then we will boil them until they are tender. Not too soft, mind you, just perfect for mashing a little later. While they are cooking, let's tend to our bacalhau. If it's salted, we must remember to soak it for a day or two, changing the water often. But if it's already desalted, even better! We will flake it into lovely pieces.

Now, grab your pan. Add a good drizzle of our golden azeite. Chop up that cebola nice and fine. Sauté it gently until it's soft and smells wonderful. Then, add the flaked bacalhau to the pan with the cebola. Let it cook for just a few minutes, until it's heated through and smells so good.

Once the batatas are cooked, drain them and mash them up a bit. Not a smooth purée, no no. We want some texture, like little clouds.

Now, my filho, the magic happens. In a separate bowl, whisk up those ovos. We'll add a little salt and pepper to the ovos, just a pinch.

Here's the trick, meu querido: Gently fold the mashed batatas into the bacalhau and cebola mixture. Then, carefully pour in the whisked ovos. Stir it all together, but gently, so we don't break up the bacalhau too much.

Pour this lovely mixture back into the pan with a little more azeite. Cook it on a low heat, stirring occasionally, until the ovos are set and everything is beautifully combined. It will be like a lovely, comforting scramble.

And there you have it! A simple, nourishing meal made with love from our frigorífico. Serve it warm, my darling. You did so well!", "gemini"]
